# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

THIRZA, who was strolling toward her house on a late April evening after an Aid meeting, felt the thrill of delight that spring always bestows upon the oldest and saddest no less than the youngest and merriest, making her aware that winter had ended and vanished. Subjective analysis regarding her thoughts and feelings was not something Thirza usually practiced. It is likely she believed her mind was occupied with the Aids, their missionary box, and the new carpet intended for the vestry room; nevertheless, beneath these ideas lay a balanced awareness of red fields steaming into pale-purply mists under the setting sun, of long, sharp-pointed fir shadows extending across the meadow past the brook, of quiet, crimson-budded maples surrounding a glass-like forest pond, of a revival throughout the earth and a movement of concealed pulses beneath the gray turf. Spring was present across the countryside, and Thirza’s calm, middle-aged stride grew lighter and quicker on account of its profound, elemental joy.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0000 }

With affectionate eyes, she gazed at Grey Shutters, which peeped out from behind its web of trees while its windowpanes threw back the sunshine in a few tiny glimmers of splendour. Navigating the soggy lane carefully, Thirza felt genuine pleasure in remembering that her return home meant a crackling log fire and a prettily laid tea table, rather than the chill solace of the former Aid meeting nights prior to Nell's arrival at Grey Shutters.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0001 }

Thus, upon stepping into her kitchen to discover the fire extinguished and Nell nowhere in sight, Thirza experienced a rightful sense of letdown and annoyance. Although she had instructed Nell to guarantee that tea was prepared for five o’clock, she was now forced to quickly shed her second-best dress and fix the food on her own before Obed came back from plowing.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0002 }

“When Miss Nell gets back, I will deal with her,” Thirza declared sternly, applying an unnecessarily forceful carving knife to slice some kindling. Having entered the room, Obed sat quietly in his spot while waiting for his tea. “Rather than giving a single thought to her chores or what time it is, she is out wandering with Isolde, engaged in silly antics like crafting tales or rehearsing dialogues. This behavior must be halted immediately and without delay. It matters little to me that Mrs. Wace claims she is the most brilliant and charming child she has ever met. Brilliant and charming she might well be, yet her mind is packed with foolish ideas, and there is no telling how her next whim will manifest. The moment she moves past one absurdity, she adopts a new one. Oh, look at me! Now I am uttering the exact sentiment that made me so angry when Agatha Sowerby expressed it at the Aid earlier. It gave me genuine pleasure when Mrs. Wace defended Nell, because had she stayed silent, I am certain I would have snapped at Agatha in front of everyone. Goodness knows Nell possesses an abundance of flaws, and I am certainly not going to pretend otherwise. However, I am the one raising her, not Agatha Sowerby, who would discover flaws in the Angel Gabriel if he were residing in Brierley. Even so, Nell ought not to have departed from the home this way after my instructions to remain here this afternoon and attend to her responsibilities. I have to admit that despite her shortcomings, she has never shown herself to be rebellious or unreliable until now, and discovering this about her makes me truly sad.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0003 }

“Well now, I dunno,” Obed remarked, since, as a patient, wise, and especially hungry man, he thought it smartest to allow Thirza to exhaust her anger without interference, knowing from past experience that she completed any present task far faster when not held up by ill-timed debate. “Perhaps you’re judging her too hasty, Thirza. Don’t call her untrustworthy until you’re sure she has disobeyed you. Mebbe it can all be explained—Nell’s a great hand at explaining.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0004 }

“When I instructed her to remain, she failed to stay here,” Thirza shot back. “Explanations for that will prove difficult for her to deliver to my liking, I suppose. Naturally, Obed, I was aware you would defend her. However, her upbringing falls on me, not you.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0005 }

The sky had grown dark by the time the evening meal was prepared, yet Nell had not appeared, rushing across the log bridge or travelling up Linger Lane, out of breath and remorseful for forgetting her chores. With a stern manner, Thirza cleaned and stored the dishes. Afterwards, needing a candle so she could see her path down to the cellar, she climbed to the east gable to fetch the one usually kept on Nell’s table. Having lit it, she spun about and discovered Nell herself resting on the bed, her face buried in the pillows.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0006 }

“Mercy on us,” Thirza said in astonishment, “Nell, have you been sleeping?”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0007 }

“No,” came the smothered answer.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0008 }

“Then are you ill?” Thirza asked with concern, moving toward the bed.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0009 }

Nell drew back further into her pillows, as though she wished to conceal herself eternally from human sight.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0010 }

“No. Thirza, I beg you to leave and turn your eyes from me. The deepest hopelessness has consumed me, and my concern for who takes top marks, composes the finest essay, or performs with the Sunday-school vocalists has completely vanished. Such trivial matters carry zero weight currently, as my ability to venture out in public ever again seems lost. I have reached the end of my life’s work. Thirza, I am asking you to depart and refrain from viewing me.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0011 }

“Has anybody ever heard such a thing?” asked the bewildered Thirza. “Nell Harcourt, what on earth is wrong with you? What did you do? Stand up right now and inform me. Right this instant, I say. Come on, what is it?”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0012 }

In hopeless submission, Nell had collapsed onto the ground.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0013 }

“Look at my hair, Thirza,” she whispered.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0014 }

Consequently, Thirza raised her light and intently examined the hair of Nell, which streamed over her back in thick waves. Indeed, it possessed a most peculiar look.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0015 }

“Nell Harcourt, what is the matter with your hair? Why, green is what it has become!”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0016 }

Were it an earthly hue, it could perhaps be termed green—a strange, drab, bronzen green, featuring occasional stripes of the initial red that intensified the gruesome appearance. At that instant, Thirza had never once in her entire existence beheld something as bizarre as the hair of Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0017 }

“Yes, it is green,” Nell groaned. “I believed that red hair was as terrible as anything could be. However, I realize now that possessing green hair is ten times more awful. Oh, Thirza, you have no idea how completely miserable I feel.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0018 }

“Although I have no idea how you ended up in this trouble, I intend to learn the reason,” Thirza stated. “Walk down to the kitchen immediately—the temperature is far too chilly up here—and explain to me precisely what has occurred on your end. For a while now, I have anticipated some odd behavior. More than two months have passed without you getting into a mess, so I was certain you were owing for another. Well, what happened to your hair?”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0019 }

“I dyed it.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0020 }

“Coloured it! Coloured your hair! Nell Harcourt, were you unaware that doing such a thing was evil?”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0021 }

“Indeed, I recognized that it was somewhat sinful,” confessed Nell. “However, I believed that committing a small sin was a price worth paying to eliminate red hair. I weighed the consequences, Thirza. Furthermore, I intended to compensate for it by being exceptionally well-behaved in different matters.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0022 }

“Well,” Thirza remarked with sarcasm, “had I chosen to make the effort to dye my hair I would have selected a respectable shade at the minimum. I would not have colored it green.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0023 }

“However, green was not the color I intended to dye it, Thirza,” Nell objected in a downcast manner. “Had my intentions been evil, I wished for them to achieve a specific result. My hair would become a gorgeous raven black according to his claim—a fact he guaranteed me with utter certainty. In what way was I to disbelieve him, Thirza? Experiencing someone disbelieving your own statement is a feeling I understand well. Furthermore, Mrs. Wace states that we ought not to mistrust a person’s honesty until evidence of their falsehood exists. That evidence is now in my possession—a green head of hair serves as sufficient evidence for anyone. Yet back at that moment, such proof was absent, and I trusted every single statement he made without reservation.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0024 }

“Who spoke? About whom are you speaking?”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0025 }

“The merchant who came by earlier today. He sold me the dye.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0026 }

“Nell Harcourt, how many times must I remind you not to permit any of those Italians inside the home! I am entirely against giving them any reason to come about.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0027 }

“Oh, I refused to allow him inside the dwelling. Recalling your advice, I stepped outside, cautiously closed the door behind me, and inspected the items he had set on the step. Furthermore, he was not an Italian—he was a German Jew. He possessed a large crate crammed with extremely fascinating goods, and he informed me that he was laboring diligently to earn sufficient funds to transport his wife and offspring over from Germany. His words regarding them were so filled with emotion that my heart was moved. I desired to purchase an item from him so I could assist him with such a noble goal. At that moment, I suddenly noticed the bottle containing hair dye. The itinerant seller claimed it was guaranteed to color any hair a lovely raven black and would not wash away. Instantly, I pictured myself possessing lovely raven-black hair, and I could not withstand the urge. However, the cost of the bottle amounted to seventy-five cents, whereas I possessed merely fifty cents remaining from my poultry earnings. I believe the itinerant seller possessed a most compassionate nature, because he stated that, because it was I, he would dispose of it for fifty cents, which amounted to simply bestowing it as a gift. Consequently, I purchased it, and the moment he departed, I mounted the stairs to this place and put it on using a former hairbrush according to the instructions. I consumed the entire bottle, and oh, Thirza, once I observed the terrible shade my hair became, I felt remorse for having been bad, I assure you. And my remorse has continued non-stop ever since.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0028 }

“Well, I hope your repentance will prove useful,” Thirza said sternly, “and that you now see clearly the place to which you have been brought by your vanity, Nell. Goodness knows what ought to be done. The initial step, I imagine, is thoroughly to wash your hair and find out whether any improvement comes from that.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0029 }

Consequently, Nell cleansed her locks, rubbing them forcefully using water and soap, yet she could just as easily have been scrubbing their native crimson for all the effect it produced. Though his honesty could be questioned on different counts, the peddler had undoubtedly stated what was true when he asserted that the dye was impossible to wash away.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0030 }

“Oh, Thirza, what am I going to do?” weeping Nell asked. “Living this down will be impossible for me. Everyone had mostly put my past errors out of mind—the cake made with liniment, making Isolde intoxicated, and losing my temper at Mrs. Sowerby. However, this is something they will always remember. My respectability will be doubted by them. Oh, Thirza, ‘when we first practice deceiving, what a tangled web we weave.’ Although that is a line of verse, it speaks the truth. And oh, the way Flossie Tulk is going to mock me! Thirza, facing Flossie Tulk is beyond me. In all of St. Brendan’s Island, no girl is more miserable than I am.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0031 }

Nell remained miserable throughout the entire week. For that duration she stayed at home and washed her hair daily. Only Isolde among those outside the family was aware of the deadly secret, yet she gave her solemn word to keep it quiet, and it can be declared right now that she honored that promise. When seven days had passed, Thirza declared with finality:
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0032 }

“Nell, it is useless. That dye is certainly permanent. Cutting off your hair is the only option left. You cannot venture outside with it in that state.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0033 }

A tremble touched Nell’s lips as the harsh reality of what Thirza said hit her. Uttering a gloomy sigh, she moved to retrieve the scissors.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0034 }

“Thirza, do shear it away this instant and get it done,” I urged. “Ah, my heart feels completely shattered. Such a mundane misfortune this is. Fever causes book heroines to shed their locks, or they sacrifice them for a worthy cause, and I know I’d mind far less if my own loss happened like that. However, finding solace when you must chop off your hair for dyeing it an appalling shade is impossible, isn't it? As long as it does not hinder you, I intend to cry continuously while you snip it away. It strikes me as terribly tragic.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0035 }

Nell cried at that time, though afterward, upon ascending the stairs and peering into the mirror, despair made her tranquil. The job had been executed meticulously by Thirza, making it essential to crop the hair as short as conceivable. To put the matter in the most understated manner, the outcome lacked beauty. Her mirror was immediately flipped to face the wall by Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0036 }

“Until my hair grows back, I will never, ever look at my reflection again,” she declared with deep emotion.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0037 }

Afterward, she abruptly set the tumbler upright again.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0038 }

“Indeed, I shall also do that. Penance is what I would perform for such wicked behavior. Every single time I enter my chamber, I will gaze at my reflection to behold my own ugliness. Furthermore, I shall refrain from attempting to erase it through my imagination. It never occurred to me that I possessed vanity regarding my hair, out of all my features, yet now I realize I truly did, despite its red hue, owing to its immense length, density, and curls. It is my expectation that my nose will be the next thing affected.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0039 }

On the next Monday, a sensation was caused at school by Nell’s clipped head, yet nobody, including Flossie Tulk, deduced why it had actually happened, much to Nell's relief; Flossie, nevertheless, made sure to tell Nell that a complete scarecrow was what she resembled.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0040 }

“When Flossie spoke those words to me, I remained silent,” Nell disclosed to Thirza later that night, as Thirza rested on the sofa following a headache, “since I believed I deserved it as part of my penance and should endure it without complaining. Being informed that you resemble a scarecrow is difficult, and I felt like replying. However, I refrained. I merely cast a single contemptuous glance her way before granting her my forgiveness. Forgiving others gives one such a sense of righteousness, wouldn’t you agree? From now on, I intend to focus entirely on leading a righteous life, and I will abandon any further attempts to look attractive. Naturally, moral goodness is superior. I am well aware of that, yet holding onto a belief can occasionally prove quite challenging despite knowing its truth. My genuine desire is to be righteous, Thirza, in the manner of yourself, Mrs. Wace, and Miss Thorne, so that I may mature into a person who brings you pride. Isolde suggests that once my hair starts coming back, I should fasten a black velvet ribbon with a bow on the side around my skull. According to her, it ought to look quite flattering. I shall refer to it as a snood, which carries such a romantic connotation. Nevertheless, is my chatter excessive, Thirza? Is it aggravating your head?”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0041 }

“My pain has eased up at present. It was dreadfully severe earlier today, however. My headaches are becoming increasingly severe. Seeing a doctor about them will be necessary for me. Regarding your talking, I am not sure that it bothers me—it has become so familiar to me.”
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0042 }

That constituted the manner in which Thirza indicated her enjoyment of listening to it.
{: #nw-v01-c27-p0043 }
